references.text: The same materials are mentioned: blue, purple, and scarlet wool, which were to be used for the sanctuary.
The curtain was also to be made of the same materials with cherubim, woven by a skilled craftsman.
The courtyard was also to have hangings of fine twisted linen.
The fulfillment of this commandment, where the craftsmen actually made the tabernacle with ten curtains.
The curtain was made with cherubim of artistic work, using the same technique as the curtains.
The ephod was also to be made of the same materials: gold, blue, purple, and scarlet wool, and fine twisted linen.
Cherubim were a recurring motif in Solomon's temple, continuing the tradition from the tabernacle.
The Epistle to the Hebrews describes the furnishings of the tabernacle and its symbolic meaning in the new covenant.
Christ passed through the greater and more perfect tent that was not made with hands, which the tabernacle pointed toward.
Shows the continuity in God's dwelling-place theology from the wilderness tabernacle to Solomon's temple through the identical design of the curtain.
